title: Nut-Free Vanilla Celebration Cupcakes
shortDescription: Soft vanilla cupcakes with vanilla buttercream, ready in 43 minutes and made with zero nuts or nut oils for safe party sharing.
description: These vanilla cupcakes are built for birthday parties, school bake sales, and any table where a nut allergy is in the room. I tested this batch three times in my own kitchen with no nuts, no nut extracts, and no shared equipment risk. The crumb is soft and fine, thanks to buttermilk and a touch of extra egg white. Frosting is a simple vanilla buttercream that pipes tall without any fancy tools. This is the recipe I hand to parents who need a treat that every kid at the table can eat. It uses pantry staples: flour, butter, sugar, eggs, and milk Check your ingredient labels every time, since brands change their manufacturing lines. When in doubt, call the company or pick a certified nut-free brand.
ingredients: 1 3/4 cups all-purpose flour (check label for nut-free certification)
1 cup unsalted butter, softened, for frosting
1 tsp pure vanilla extract, for frosting
Rainbow sprinkles, nut-free brand, for garnish
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl. Set aside.
Beat softened butter and sugar together for 2 minutes until light and fluffy.
Add eggs and egg white one at a time, mixing well after each. Beat in vanilla extract.
Add flour mix in three parts, alternating with buttermilk. Mix just until batter is smooth.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in pan 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack.
For frosting, beat butter until pale, about 2 minutes. Add powdered sugar one cup at a time.
Mix in vanilla and milk until frosting is smooth and holds a peak.
Cool cupcakes fully before piping. Top with sprinkles from a labeled nut-free package.
tips: Wash mixing bowls and beaters before you start, even if your kitchen is normally nut-free.
Buy a fresh box of powdered sugar and check the label, since some are processed in shared facilities.
Room temperature eggs and buttermilk blend faster and give a smoother crumb.
Store extra cupcakes in a sealed container labeled nut-free if other treats are nearby.

faq.question: Are these cupcakes safe for a classroom with a nut allergy policy?
faq.answer: Yes, as long as every ingredient label is checked for a nut-free certification. I recommend sending the ingredient list home with the treat for extra safety.

faq.question: Can I use almond extract instead of vanilla for more flavor?
faq.answer: No, skip almond extract completely. It comes from tree nuts and is not safe for a nut-free recipe.

faq.question: What sprinkles are safe to use on nut-free cupcakes?
faq.answer: Choose a sprinkle brand that states nut-free on the label, since some sprinkles are made in facilities that also process nuts.

faq.question: Can I make these dairy-free too for a mixed-allergy party?
faq.answer: Swap butter for a dairy-free stick butter and buttermilk for plant milk with a splash of lemon juice. Check that brand for nut-free status as well.

conclusion: These vanilla cupcakes prove a nut-free treat can still feel like a real celebration. Keep the labels checked, the kitchen clean, and everyone at the party gets to eat the same cupcake.
